_about: Short local reasons for the by-design and not-expressible cases of the service-by-design table, keyed by case id: one short sentence (a clause, or two joined by ';' where the host refuses too, with its own text; up to about 45 words, where the owner's own example is eight: 'query exceeds the service's supported length') the tables print in a not-exercised MCP cell, under a normalised row, in a detail block's adjudication line and as 'in short' in appendix B (the long explanation stays in appendix B; the generator adds the class in words, the service's status and code and the pointer 'see B' itself). `verification`, keyed the same way, is the rule by which a case's pairs are verified or not, for a case whose rule is its own (the deadline relayed as a failed task): appendix B prints it under the case's short reason and nowhere else, so that the short reason stays short (VERIFY-FINAL R2; VERIFY-FIX2 L1: the reasons the owner's chapter R reviews passed are sentences, not clauses, so the rule is one short sentence, bounded by tests/test_doc.py at 50 words and two clauses). Plain text, inline markup `code` and *emphasis*. A case without an entry falls back on the manifest's not-implemented reason, the case's missing argument or its service outcome. Written for the cases chapter R names (2026-10-15), extended with every case the other chapters name in manifests v4 and v5 (their prose writers' reasons, one per case).

_assumes._note: The literal numbers this file's prose may carry, each with its source: constants of the SPEC, of the manifest v4 (lengths, budgets, expected runs), of the service's table or of the harness, never a figure of a run (those are placeholders the generator fills). tests/test_doc.py fails on a number the prose carries that is listed neither here nor as a placeholder; add a constant here with its source, never a run's figure.
_assumes.10: the tool's inline wait for a discovery, 10 s (service_by_design.json)
_assumes.30: the tool's inline wait with explicit labels, 30 s (service_by_design.json)
_assumes.60: about 60 s, the service's default budget as seconds (service_by_design.json)
_assumes.250: the finalisation reserve in ms (SPEC section 4.5)
_assumes.400: http 400 (SPEC; the service's refusals); the service's refusals, service_by_design.json)
_assumes.500: a discovery's 500 bp and the service's minimum budget of 500 ms (service_by_design.json); the service's minimum budget of 500 ms (service_by_design.json pattern.time_budget_below_minimum)
_assumes.502: http 502 backend_fault (service_by_design.json); http 502, the MCP normaliser's rendering of a failed search (service_by_design.json pattern.deadline_ends_task); http 502 `search_failed`, the suite's rendering of the service's failed search (service_by_design.json pattern.deadline_ends_task)
_assumes.503: http 503 deadline (SPEC section 4.5); http 503 deadline (SPEC section 7.6); http 503 deadline (SPEC-pattern-search section 6)
_assumes.1,000: the service's cap of 1,000 distinct labels (service_by_design.json); the service's maximum `max_live_paths` (service_by_design.json service_maxima); the service's limit of 1,000 characters on a pattern (service_by_design.json pattern.length_above_1000); the service's discovery cap of 1,000 since manifest v5 (service_by_design.json resolve.discover_limit_above_cap)
_assumes.10,000: the server's max_query_bp (host_capabilities); the service's maximum `max_extension_bp` and `max_paths` (service_by_design.json service_maxima); the service's ceiling and the host's cap on max_contexts (service_by_design.json pattern.max_contexts_above_10000)
_assumes.4: the host's `max_seeds` on staging (service_by_design.json traverse.seeds_above_host_max_seeds; host capabilities); max_mismatches 4 (manifest M-refusal-0001)
_assumes.15,000: the walk preset's budget row in ms (service_by_design.json presets)
_assumes.30,000: the trie preset's budget row in ms (service_by_design.json presets)
_assumes.0: a cap of 0 and max_mismatches 0 (service_by_design.json pattern.caps_zero, mismatch.zero); the cap 0 of a pattern longer than k (SPEC section 21.16)
_assumes.1: 1, the value the SDK coerces a string or true to (service_by_design.json mismatch.value_string_1, mismatch.value_true); the protein cap of 1 on staging (host capabilities mismatches.max.protein); 1 .. the list's length, the range of at_least's n (SPEC-pattern-search section 19.3)
_assumes.16: the service's chunk of 16 patterns (service_by_design.json pattern.too_many_patterns_chunked)

short.resolve.not_expressible.bounds_max_query: the tool always sends its own `bounds.max_query_bp` (2,000; 500 for a discovery) and has no argument for another
short.resolve.not_expressible.support: the tool has no support argument
short.resolve.not_expressible.graph: the tool has no graph argument
short.resolve.not_expressible.select: the tool has no select argument
short.capabilities.not_expressible.protocol: the tool builds the HTTP request itself, so a raw body, a header or a method cannot be chosen
short.resolve.sequence_too_long: the service answers 400 `resolve_query_too_long` (a resolve takes at most 2,000 bp) at submit, so the host's own limit of 10,000 bp is never reached
short.resolve.sequence_too_short: the host's 400 (Query shorter than k) comes back as 502 `backend_fault` with the host's text
short.resolve.unknown_label: the host's 400 (Label not found in the annotation) comes back as 400 `resolve_rejected` with the host's text
short.resolve.duplicate_labels: the service de-duplicates the labels before the request, so the host sees one label and answers 200 where the direct request is refused with Duplicate label
short.resolve.lowercase_whitespace_fasta: the service upper-cases the sequence (and strips whitespace and a FASTA header) before the request; the answers agree
short.resolve.n_or_iupac: the service answers 400 `resolve_sequence_invalid` (a character outside ACGT) at submit, where the host answers 200 with the k-mers holding the code absent from the graph
short.resolve.too_many_labels: the service answers 400 `resolve_too_many_labels` (at most 1,000 distinct labels) at submit, where the host has no cap
short.resolve.empty_sequence: the service's own validation answers `invalid_arguments` (provide a sequence) before any request; the host refuses too, with its own text
short.resolve.discover_with_labels: the service's own validation answers `invalid_arguments` (either labels or discover, not both); the host refuses too, with its own text
short.resolve.no_labels_no_discover: the service's own validation answers `resolve_labels_required`; the host refuses too, with its own text
short.resolve.time_budget_below_minimum: the service answers 400 `resolve_time_budget_out_of_bounds` (below its minimum of 500 ms) at submit; the host refuses too, a budget not above the 250 ms reserve
short.resolve.time_budget_above_host_max: the service answers 400 `resolve_time_budget_out_of_bounds` (above the host's cap) at submit, where the host lowers the budget to its cap and states it (clamped)
short.resolve.time_budget_above_reserve_below_: the service answers 400 `resolve_time_budget_out_of_bounds` (below its minimum of 500 ms) at submit, where the host answers (a 200, or a 503 deadline under load)
short.resolve.discover_limit_above_100: the service's own validation answers `invalid_arguments` (the limit must be in 1..100); the host refuses too (out of range)
short.resolve.discover_limit_above_100_host_an: the service's own validation answers `invalid_arguments` (the limit must be in 1..100), where the host answers 200 (its own cap is far higher)
short.resolve.discover_limit_above_cap: the service's own validation answers `invalid_arguments` (the limit must be in 1 to 1,000, the service's discovery cap since manifest v5); the host refuses too (out of range)
short.resolve.discover_limit_above_cap_host_an: the service's own validation answers `invalid_arguments` (the limit must be in 1 to 1,000, the service's discovery cap since manifest v5), where the host answers 200 (it has no discovery cap of its own)
short.resolve.discovery_too_long: the service answers 400 `resolve_query_too_long` (a discovery takes at most 500 bp) at submit, where the host answers
short.resolve.blank_label: the service's own validation answers `invalid_arguments` (a blank label)
short.resolve.time_budget_unnamed: the tool sends `bounds.time_budget_ms` 60,000 where the request names none, so a resolve needing more than about 60 s answers a stated stop via MCP and completes directly; the profile checks read the prefix
short.resolve.job_path: the service runs the resolve in its queue and the tool waits inline (30 s with explicit labels, 10 s for a discovery) or hands back the job; no difference in the answer
short.service.resolve_repeat: on the anonymous path each call is a new resolve job (with an API key the service may return the running or recent job instead); no difference in the answer
short.traverse.bounds_budget_above_preset_row: the service refuses a time, memory or work budget above its preset's row (walk 15,000 ms / 512 MB / 100,000,000 units, trie 30,000 ms) at submit (400 `strategy_out_of_bounds`), where the host lowers a time budget to its cap and states it (clamped)
short.traverse.bounds_knob_above_service_maxim: the service refuses a bound above its own maximum (`max_live_paths` 1,000, `max_extension_bp` 10,000, `max_paths` 10,000, `max_output_bp` 2,000,000, `max_steps` 1,000,000) at submit (400 `strategy_out_of_bounds`), where the host walks it under its own limits
short.traverse.duplicate_seeds: the service merges identical seeds onto the first before sending, so the host sees one seed and answers one result where the direct request gets two, the second marked duplicate; the comparison reads the one result for two seeds (one distinct) by the table
short.traverse.empty_seed_labels: the service answers 400 `seed_invalid` (an explicitly empty labels list permits nothing) at submit; the host refuses too, with its own text
short.traverse.empty_seeds: the tool's own validation answers `invalid_arguments` (provide seeds) before any request; the host refuses too, with its own text
short.traverse.not_expressible.advanced_strate: annotate mode, a beam and any strategy outside the presets have no tool argument (the advanced presets are not enabled on this deployment)
short.traverse.not_expressible.attempt_fields: the attempt fields (`attempt_id`, `budget_id`, `locus_id`, `not_after_ms`, `expect_server_instance`) are the service's own, sent by its worker; the caller cannot set them
short.traverse.not_expressible.graph: the tool has no graph argument (nor graphs or graph_path); the service never sends one to a single-graph host
short.traverse.not_expressible.non_object_body: the tool always builds a JSON object body, so a non-object body cannot be sent
short.traverse.not_expressible.strategy_keys: the tool's overrides are bounds, direction, exhaustive, `labels.max_labels_per_node` and `labels.seed_label_kind`; any other strategy key (`labels.mode`, a branching, frontier, output or annotation key) is refused by the tool naming it (`preset_unavailable`, the advanced strategy path) or has no argument
short.traverse.seed_shorter_than_k: the service answers 400 `seed_invalid` (shorter than k = 31) at submit; the host refuses too, with its own text
short.traverse.seed_with_n_or_iupac: the service answers 400 `seed_invalid` (a character outside ACGT) at submit; the host refuses too, naming the position
short.traverse.seeds_above_host_max_seeds: the service batches the seeds into host requests of at most the host's `max_seeds` (4 on staging), so the host answers the 5 seeds in two requests where the direct request is refused; the comparison reads the status by the table
short.traverse.trace_preset: the trace preset (`support` trace, `on_reconverge` keep) is accepted by the tool, although its docstring names walk and trie only; `output.coordinates` cannot be set
short.traverse.unknown_bounds_key: an unknown key inside bounds passes the tool (bounds is whitelisted whole) and the host's 400 comes back relayed as `backend_rejected` with the host's text
short.traverse.unknown_strategy_key: a key outside the tool's overrides is refused by the tool naming it (`preset_unavailable`, the advanced strategy path) before any request; the host refuses too, with its own text
short.traverse.advanced_path_disabled: `labels.max_seed_labels` is on the advanced strategy path, which this deployment does not enable: the tool refuses it (`preset_unavailable`) before any request
short.pattern.bad_alphabet_dna: the service answers 400 `pattern_invalid` (a character outside A, C, G, T) at submit for the whole request, where the host refuses that pattern's slot alone (`bad_alphabet`) and answers the others
short.pattern.bad_alphabet_iupac: the service answers 400 `pattern_invalid` (a character outside the 15 IUPAC codes) at submit for the whole request, where the host refuses the slot alone
short.pattern.u_for_t: the service answers 400 `pattern_invalid` for a U at submit and never rewrites U to T, where the host refuses the slot alone (`bad_alphabet`)
short.pattern.empty_pattern_string: the service answers 400 `pattern_invalid` (the pattern is empty) at submit for the whole request, where the host refuses the slot alone with the message `pattern: empty`
short.pattern.empty_pattern_list: the tool's own validation answers `invalid_arguments` (a non-empty list of patterns) before any request; the host refuses too, with its own text
short.pattern.too_many_patterns_chunked: the service splits 17 patterns into chunks of 16 and answers every pattern through two host requests, where one direct request of 17 is refused 400 (never cut)
short.pattern.duplicate_ids: the service answers 400 `pattern_invalid` (an id used twice) at submit, where the host echoes the ids and answers both
short.pattern.lowercase: the service upper-cases the pattern before the request, so the host never sees lower case from the MCP arm; the answers agree
short.pattern.unknown_field: the tool has no such argument, and an extra argument is dropped by the MCP SDK without an error, so the request cannot be sent as the host would refuse it
short.pattern.max_contexts_above_10000: the service answers 400 `pattern_out_of_bounds` (`caps.max_contexts` above 10,000) at submit, where the host lowers the value to its cap and lists it in `limits.clamped`
short.pattern.caps_zero: the service's request model takes every cap as at least 1 and answers 400 `pattern_invalid` at submit, where the host accepts `max_contexts`, `max_anchors` and `max_paths` 0 and answers (a cut, a withheld list, no extension)
short.pattern.not_expressible.stop_at_threshol: the tool has no `stop_at_threshold` argument (the service never sends it)
short.pattern.not_expressible.max_steps: the tool has no `max_steps` argument; sent as an extra argument it would be dropped and the search run without it
short.pattern.not_expressible.budget_split: the tool has no `budget_split` argument (the host refuses the field as a later increment)
short.pattern.not_expressible.graphs: the tool has no `graphs` argument; the service sends `graphs` only to a chunked database's task, never to this single-graph host
short.pattern.occurrences_without_labels: the service answers 400 `pattern_invalid` (occurrences need labels `all` or `predicate_only`) at submit; the host refuses too, with its own text
short.pattern.two_kinds_in_one_pattern: the service's request model answers 400 `pattern_invalid` (a pattern names exactly one of dna, iupac, protein) at submit; the host refuses too, with its own text
short.pattern.in_ram_by_size: the service sends `in_ram: true` only for a request whose patterns exceed its size threshold; a single-graph host answers from the index it holds either way (`timing.load_ms` 0), so the answers agree
short.pattern.strands_vocabulary: the tool's strand words are both / plus / minus, mapped to the host's both / forward / reverse before the request (forward or reverse sent as such is refused 400 `pattern_invalid`); the answers agree, but the tool's answer does not echo an entry's `strands`
short.pattern.time_budget_below_minimum: the service answers 400 `pattern_out_of_bounds` (a budget below its minimum of 500 ms) at submit, where the host accepts a budget above its reserve and answers (a 200 with stated time stops, or a 503 deadline)
short.pattern.length_above_1000: the service answers 400 `pattern_invalid` (a pattern of more than 1,000 characters) at submit whatever `long_search` says, where the host has no length cap and extends the pattern into its paths
short.pattern.long_without_long_search: the service answers 400 `pattern_invalid` (more than k bases without `long_search`) at submit, where the host answers the anchors alone with the paths withheld `paths_later_increment`, or with `max_mismatches` above 0 that pattern's slot `mismatches_above_cap` with the cap 0
short.pattern.not_expressible.max_annotation_w: the tool has no `max_annotation_work` argument (the service never sends it); the host's default applies
short.pattern.not_expressible.max_memory_mb: the tool has no `max_memory_mb` argument; the host's default applies
short.pattern.genetic_code_unknown: the service answers 400 `pattern_invalid` (a genetic code the host does not serve) at submit; the host refuses too, 400 `genetic_code_unknown` with its own text
short.pattern.protein_alphabet: the service answers 400 `pattern_invalid` (a character outside the host's protein residues) at submit for the whole request, where the host refuses the slot alone (`bad_alphabet`) and answers the other peptide
short.pattern.deadline_ends_task: the host's /pattern 503 deadline ends the service's task at once and comes back as 502 `search_failed` (`pattern_deadline`)
short.mismatch.value_4: the tool sends 4 and the service's request model answers 400 `pattern_invalid` (an integer from 0 to 3) at submit; the host refuses too, with its own text
short.mismatch.value_minus_1: the tool sends -1 and the service's request model answers 400 `pattern_invalid` (an integer from 0 to 3) at submit; the host refuses too, with its own text
short.mismatch.value_1_5: the MCP SDK's argument validation refuses 1.5 (not a valid integer) before the tool runs, with no structured code; the host's 400 cannot be asked for through the tools
short.mismatch.value_string_1: the MCP SDK coerces the string `1` to 1, so the tool sends 1 and the search runs with one substitution where the host refuses the string
short.mismatch.value_null: `null` is the tool argument's default: nothing is sent and the search is exact, where the host refuses an explicit null
short.mismatch.value_true: the MCP SDK coerces `true` to 1, so the search runs with one substitution where the host refuses the boolean
short.mismatch.zero: 0 is never sent: the host receives the request without the field, byte for byte the exact request, so the direct arm's explicit 0 and the MCP arm's absent field answer alike
short.mismatch.above_kind_cap: the service answers 400 `pattern_out_of_bounds` (above the host's cap for that kind: 1 for protein on staging) at submit for the whole request, where the host answers that pattern's slot `mismatches_above_cap` and the others
short.mismatch.long_pattern_without_long_searc: the service answers 400 `pattern_invalid` (more than k bases without `long_search`) at submit, before it looks at substitutions, where the host answers the long pattern's slot `mismatches_above_cap` with the cap 0 and the others
short.mismatch.long_pattern_with_long_search: the service answers 400 `pattern_unsupported` (substitutions in a pattern longer than k are a later increment on its host) at submit for the whole request, where the host answers that pattern's slot `mismatches_above_cap` with the cap 0 and the others
short.mismatch.with_labels: the service answers 400 `pattern_unsupported` (`max_mismatches` above 0 with labels is a later increment on its host) at submit; the host refuses too, 400 `later_increment` with its own text
short.mismatch.with_predicate: the service answers 400 `pattern_unsupported` (`max_mismatches` above 0 with a predicate is a later increment on its host) at submit; the host refuses too, 400 `later_increment` with its own text
short.mismatch.with_supported_paths: the service answers 400 `pattern_unsupported` (`max_mismatches` above 0 with `supported_paths` is a later increment on its host) at submit; the host refuses too, 400 `later_increment` with its own text
short.pattern.predicate_name_not_string: the service answers 400 `pattern_invalid` at submit (a name is a string: `write a taxid as "562"`), naming the path of the fault; the host refuses too, with its own `invalid_request` text
short.pattern.predicate_only_without_predicate: the service answers 400 `pattern_invalid` at submit (labels predicate_only returns the labels a predicate names, so it needs a predicate); the host refuses too, with its own text
short.pattern.predicate_form_other: the service answers 400 `pattern_invalid` at submit, naming the path of the first form fault (here `at_least.n` outside 1 .. the list's length); the host refuses too, with its own text
short.pattern.predicate_options_without_predic: the service answers 400 `pattern_invalid` at submit (predicate_scope motif acts only with a predicate); the host refuses too, with its own text naming `predicate_scope`
short.pattern.predicate_options_noop_without_p: the service answers 400 `pattern_invalid` at submit (predicate_strands acts only with a predicate), where the host accepts the field as a no-op and answers 200
short.capabilities.traverse_capabilities_docum: the `traverse_capabilities` tool answers the service's own view of the host (its gate, backends, service maxima and presets, cached up to an hour), not the host's document: the identity and limit fields the check reads are not exposed
short.capabilities.pattern_capabilities_docume: no tool returns the pattern block (`catalog` states per database only whether pattern search is supported and why not); the service's REST route for it is not an MCP tool
short.capabilities.server_capabilities_documen: the `traverse_capabilities` tool reshapes the host's /capabilities into its backend entry (identity, limits, feature level, resolve bounds), not the raw document, and `catalog` says per database only whether pattern search is supported: no features list, no server_instance, no size to check
short.service.pattern_repeat_reuses_search: the service may answer a repeated identical search with the running or recent one; the MCP runner names an idempotency key per execution, so each repeat is a new search and no reuse applies

verification.pattern.deadline_ends_task: the pair is verified where a direct arm answered the 503 too and the other MCP repeat, when there is one, agrees with the direct arms, and unverified where no direct arm answered the 503 (a 200 within its budget: a timing difference, not a disagreement) or where the other repeat's 200 has no direct 200 to compare with
